### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s).

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0892a94d8e190b7547408d1a37e49ba087ddd635`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0892a94d8e190b7547408d1a37e49ba087ddd635` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fecb7c1d82be1586b19deba7fa4a10354815e7a9` — the merge of head `385ecdcc7e7a0d9d47b50bd146a9da0dbea814e9` into base `0892a94d8e190b7547408d1a37e49ba087ddd635`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fecb7c1d82be1586b19deba7fa4a10354815e7a9 && git checkout fecb7c1d82be1586b19deba7fa4a10354815e7a9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0892a94d8e190b7547408d1a37e49ba087ddd635 385ecdcc7e7a0d9d47b50bd146a9da0dbea814e9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0892a94d8e190b7547408d1a37e49ba087ddd635 && git merge --no-ff 385ecdcc7e7a0d9d47b50bd146a9da0dbea814e9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0892a94d8e190b7547408d1a37e49ba087ddd635
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0892a94d8e190b7547408d1a37e49ba087ddd635` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `385ecdcc7e7a0d9d47b50bd146a9da0dbea814e9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/boot-sign-in-reachability.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-actor-guards.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/organization-delete.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-client-secret.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/tsup.config.ts, tsconfig.base.json, packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, .changeset/30300-keep-the-last-identity-provider.md and content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx (prose faces, read for the `Skills-docs:` and docs-accuracy judgments only)

Face: narrowing. No path of the diff is a published schema or a governed path; the line-initial `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and in the changeset puts the review on the narrowing face, so the scope floor is every diff path outside the prose faces, all six named above. PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed. No `Contract-review-claim`, hold or record on this head at read time (PR thread: the docs-drift bot comment only). Card thread read: 6650883232 (triage), 6651638125 (seat claim, `Clause-②: no — the dev re-measures`), 6652003986 (measurement report), 6657245276 (os-dev report). The merge base with `origin/main` is `7d7babb1`; `main` has since moved `auth-manager.ts` only by #30107 (`getPublicConfig().features.emailDelivery`, L2790/L4701), nowhere near this PR's hunks.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The narrowing itself (correct, as declared).** `sign-in-method-floor.ts#ssoProviderDeleteRefusal` refuses `POST /sso/delete-provider` only when all four hold, in this order: `publicConfig().emailPassword.enabled === false` (anything else passes), `features.sso === true` (`auth-manager.ts#isSsoWired` is the switch alone, so with enterprise SSO off the rows sign nobody in and the delete passes), `otherSignInMethods(deps, { withoutEnterpriseSso: true })` empty (a social or OIDC provider with a credential pair, phone-number sign-in, a host handoff each pass it), and `probeOtherSsoProviders` answering `absent`. The probe reads two rows of `sys_sso_provider` under `isSystem` (same `find(object, { limit }, { context: { isSystem: true } })` shape as `boot-sign-in-reachability.ts#probeSsoProvidersPresence`): zero rows is `not_found` (pass, the vendor's 404), any row with another `provider_id` is `present` (pass), a read fault or no engine is `unknown`. The 409 is the exact accept-set change the card asks for; nothing outside it moves. Judged right.
2. **Where it runs: before the vendor's first write.** `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts` L768-798 installs `globalBeforeHook` as better-auth's `hooks.before`, so `auth-manager-before-hook.ts#globalBeforeHook` L316-319 runs ahead of `@better-auth/sso`'s handler, which deletes the provider row and its linked account rows. The branch sits after the ADR-0069 D3 held-caller refusal (same path, same `fall through` comment) and before the ADR-0135 D6 registration gate (`/sso/register` only). A refused delete writes nothing; the composition test asserts the row is still there after both the zh-CN and en refusal.
3. **What stays the vendor's answer.** `auth-manager.ts#assertSsoProviderDeletable` returns before judging when no judge is set (a manager no plugin composed), when `body.providerId` is not a string (the vendor's 400), and when `resolveActor` finds no `userId` (the vendor's 401). An unknown `providerId` passes either way: with other rows the probe reads `present`, with none `not_found`, so the vendor's 404 stands (pinned, `remove('nobody')` → 404 with one `okta` row). The vendor's own provider-access check still runs after the pass. The 401/404 controls are pinned through the real endpoint.
4. **Can a valid or non-last delete be wrongly refused?** Not within the floor's own vocabulary: with two rows the first delete passes and the one left is then refused (pinned); email and password on passes; SSO off passes; each of the three other methods passes (seven `it.each` cases at the judge). The one population that is refused while another door exists is the one #30298 already does not count — `ssoOnlyMode` alone, magic link, passkeys (`sign-in-method-floor.ts` module docblock "Not counted") — so the delete door is consistent with the save door, and the refusal message names the recovery (turn email and password on first). Not a defect of this diff; the floor's counting is #30298's landed contract.
5. **The 503 fail-closed path.** `unknown` answers `{ status: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE', code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE' }`, never a pass; the judge test pins it on a throwing engine. Both status names are the ones `auth-manager-actor-guards.ts` already throws for the organization delete (`new APIError('SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE', …)` L98/L227, `new APIError('CONFLICT', { code: ORGANIZATION_DELETE_REFUSAL_CODE, … })` L320), so the 409/503 mapping and the extra body field (`lastSignInMethod`, as `dependents` there) are a known-good shape. Both codes are existing `StandardErrorCode` members (`packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts` L97 `DELETE_RESTRICTED`, L113 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`): no new error code, so no ledger entry is owed. Note: the settings floor reads an `unknown` provider table as "no row" (does not count it), the delete door reads it as 503. The two directions are both fail-closed for their door (a save that cannot prove a way in is refused; a delete that cannot prove another way in is refused), so they agree in effect.
6. **Race between two concurrent deletes of the last two rows.** Both probes can read two rows, both answer `present`, both pass, and the table ends empty. The probe and the vendor's delete are not one transaction, so the window is real. It does not change the verdict: it needs two administrators deleting within the same request window, the settings door of #30298 has the identical window (a save judged while a delete is in flight), door 2 reports the result at the next boot, and the recovery (`OS_AUTH_EMAIL_PASSWORD_ENABLED=true`) is unchanged. A follow-up card is the right carrier if the seat wants it closed (the vendor's `guardProviderMutation` seam the dev read in 6652003986 would need adapter transactions).
7. **Door 2 (report only, as ruled).** `sign-in-method-floor.ts#resolveNoSignInMethodReport` returns a message only when email and password is off, no other method counts, and (SSO off, or SSO on with the provider table READ and empty): an `unknown` probe with SSO on returns `null`. `reportIfNoSignInMethodAtBoot` catches a throwing resolver and a throwing sink, logs once at `error` (or `warn` on a sink without `error`, the `boot-sign-in-reachability.ts` convention), and returns. The `kernel:ready` site in `auth-plugin.ts` L1532-1541 awaits `ensureAuthSettingsBound` inside a `try` (that memoized call is already made unconditionally by the sibling hook at L1143, so no new binding trigger is introduced) and then the report; nothing in the path can reject the hook, so the boot is never refused. The composition test asserts the boot completes and one report line with the token and the recovery; the control (`GOOGLE_CLIENT_*` set) and the recovery (`OS_AUTH_EMAIL_PASSWORD_ENABLED=true`) assert silence. Holds the ruling.
8. **Public surface of `@objectstack/plugin-auth`: widened by one method and one reachable type.** `index.ts` L34 publishes `AuthManager` by name through the `"."` entry (`package.json` `exports`, `dist/index.d.ts`); `tsconfig.base.json` sets `declaration: true` and no `stripInternal`, `tsup.config.ts` runs plain `dts`, and the repo has no api-extractor, so `@internal` is a doc tag only and `setSsoProviderDeleteFloor(judge: (providerId, locale?) => Promise<SsoProviderDeleteRefusal | undefined>)` is emitted on the published class, carrying `SsoProviderDeleteRefusal` with it through the parameter's return type (execution-duties 〈认领〉: public surface = what the built entry declarations reach, including types reachable through props, parameters and returns). `sign-in-method-floor.ts` itself is not re-exported from `index.ts`, so the new `otherSignInMethods` option, `probeOtherSsoProviders`, `SSO_PROVIDER_DELETE_PATH`, `NO_SIGN_IN_METHOD_AT_BOOT` and the two report functions are shipped bytes, not published. Hence `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the right line: a widening (the setter and its type) plus a narrowing (the 409). `no (narrowing)` would be right only if the method were trimmed from the declarations or private, and neither is the case. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no key, value, type or default an author writes moves (`sys_sso_provider` keeps its columns; the endpoint keeps its request shape).
9. **i18n.** `SIGN_IN_FLOOR_COPY` gains `enterpriseSso` and `enterpriseSsoUnverified` in all four locales (en, zh-CN, ja-JP, es-ES); `SignInFloorCopy` makes both required, so a missing locale would not compile. `signInFloorCopy(locale)` resolves exact, then language, then en; the hook hands it `preferredLocaleFromHeader(acceptLanguageHeader(ctx))`, the reader REST already uses. Pinned: zh-CN by header, en by default, ja-JP and es-ES at the judge.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/30300-keep-the-last-identity-provider.md`: `'@objectstack/plugin-auth': patch` on the one released package the diff moves (`package.json` has no `private` field); title `fix(plugin-auth)!:`; `**BREAKING**` banner; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — …`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and `Skills-docs: none — …` line-initial in both the changeset and the PR body (`Clause-②` is read as the first token after the colon, arm in parentheses, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`); exactly one `<!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) … -->` marker, the grammar `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` L62-63 reads. Against AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition — `patch` ✓, banner ✓, disposition ✓; nothing an author writes is removed or renamed, so no FROM → TO line or `retiredKey()` is owed. Same spelling and level as #30298's `.changeset/30202-keep-a-sign-in-method.md` (patch, `yes (narrowing)`, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), the precedent for this family. `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` are `success` on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **`Skills-docs:` line — present, well-spelled, true.** `Skills-docs: none — no file under \`skills/**\` teaches deleting an SSO provider or the sign-in boot reports; \`content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx\` gains "No sign-in method left".` is the `none — REASON` arm (pm-dispatch SKILL.md L313), owed because the arm is `(narrowing)`. The docs page it names is in the diff: a three-row table (settings save → `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION` at the field, which is what `service-settings`' route tests pin for a write-predicate refusal; the delete → `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` / `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`; the redeploy → boots, `error` under `no_sign_in_method_at_boot`), the "not refused" sentence, and the recovery with the env override's precedence. Each sentence agrees with the code read in ①. Accurate.
2. **Dev `open_questions` — Clause-② re-declared `yes (narrowing)` against the seat's `no`: option A is right.** The seat's claim line reasoned that a refused delete "narrows nothing an author writes", which is the `Metadata-protocol` question, not the Clause-② one (〈认领〉: "本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗"). Measured: `200` before, `409` after at a published endpoint (the narrowing arm), and a published class gains a method (the `yes`). ①.8 carries the reading. The seat's claim comment stands as written (it said the dev re-measures); nothing to edit there.
3. **Refusal tests assert `code` and `status`?** The 409 does, through the real endpoint: `res.status` 409 and `toMatchObject({ code: 'DELETE_RESTRICTED', message, lastSignInMethod })`, twice (zh-CN, en), plus the two-row control's second delete. The 503 is asserted at the judge (`status: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE'`, `code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE'`), not over HTTP, because the composition cannot make the fault; the one `APIError(refusal.status, { code: refusal.code, … })` line is shared with the HTTP-pinned 409, and the same status word is the organization delete's 503. Acceptable; the seat may note it in ACCEPT, no REWORK.
4. **Door 2 holds ruling A.** Report only, positive claim only, never refuses (①.7). The refuse-by-posture option is named in the PR body and the module docblock as a later option, not done, with the reason (`ssoOnlyMode` tenants).
5. **`!` and `(narrowing)` battery.** `dogfood_battery` in 6657245276 is pinned to `385ecdcc`, full (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test`, 419/422 files, 3492 passed, 36 skipped, no failure). The seat verifies the check-runs, not this record.
6. **Check-runs at read time (2026-11-05 ~12:00Z):** `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Auto Label` are `success`; `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Test Core (1-8/8)` still `in_progress`. The queue entry waits for all-green (contract-review.md ②); this record does not stand in for it.
7. **Collision note (seat 2 in-flight work; branches not fetched, hunk headers read off the REST file list).** PR #30447 (#30312, `bindAuthSettings`/`applySettings`) touches `auth-plugin.ts` at main L794-806 (the `init()` lines where this PR inserts `setSsoProviderDeleteFloor` right after `this.effectiveSecondaryStorage = …`), L2103-2134 (the `registerSignInMethodFloor(settings, {…}, ctx.logger)` block this PR collapses into `registerSignInMethodFloor(settings, this.signInMethodFloorDeps(ctx, this.authManager), ctx.logger)`, and the `applySettings` opening), and `sign-in-method-floor.ts` at main L57-66 (the module docblock tail, where this PR appends the "two doors that are not a settings save" section): three textual overlaps, each a short hunk, whichever lands second rebases. #30447's other hunks (`auth-plugin.ts` L547, L2328-2560; `sign-in-method-floor.ts` L97-100 `SignInMethodFloorDeps`, L335-344 `signInMethodFloorPredicate`) do not meet this PR. #30411 (organization require-MFA refusal copy) has no open PR yet; it will touch `auth-manager.ts`, where this PR's hunks are the import block (L82-85), the setter after `setOrganizationDeleteStandingJudge` (L1588-1605), the before-hook host map (L1761), and `assertSsoProviderDeletable` after `assertOrganizationDeletable` (L5055-5083): overlap only if #30411 edits those four spots. `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts` and `auth-manager-before-hook.ts` have no in-flight sibling named.
8. **Dev's out-of-scope finding** (Setup's Register SAML Provider bridge 400) is already #30352 by the seat; nothing new to file.

### ④ Design judgment

- **`sign-in-method-floor.ts` — the delete door reuses the floor rather than copying it, as the card asks.** `ssoProviderDeleteRefusal` asks `otherSignInMethods` with the new `withoutEnterpriseSso` option and judges the provider rows itself with a bounded two-row read, so "another way in" is one list for the save, the delete and the boot, and the delete's own question ("is this the last row?") is answered without a count. `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` is the standard code for a delete refused while something depends on the row (the organization delete's), and `503` for a guard that could not be evaluated is the same module's precedent (#25059). `resolveNoSignInMethodReport` is a positive claim in the exact shape of `no_sign_in_account_at_boot` beside it. The module docblock records both measurements (`main` `bfca0efb`) and why door 2 does not refuse. Holds against the code it cites and the two measured scenarios.
- **`auth-manager-before-hook.ts` / `auth-manager.ts` / `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts` — the right seam.** The before-hook is the one place the vendor's delete can be stopped before its write (its `beforeDelete` would run inside the vendor's transaction-less handler); the host-map pattern (`BeforeHookHost`, `AuthInstanceHost`) is the file's own convention for every other guard. The judge is handed to the manager by `AuthPlugin` because the manager does not hold the host handoff or the boot credential index; `setSsoProviderDeleteFloor` mirrors `setOrganizationDeleteStandingJudge`. The `@internal` tag is honest about intent, but ①.8 stands: it does not trim the declaration, so the PR's `yes` is the right word.
- **`auth-plugin.ts` — one builder, three doors.** `signInMethodFloorDeps` replaces the inline deps object with a method used by the save, the delete and the boot report, so the three cannot drift (the card's "applied at every door"). The `kernel:ready` placement, after the account report and after the settings are bound, is where the live manager reflects the stored `email_password_enabled`; the test for the stored-false case (`settings.setMany` then a redeploy) exercises it on the real composition.
- **`sign-in-method-floor.test.ts` — the pins carry the scenario.** Two new top-level `describe`s in the floor's shared harness (ruling 6583487846): the real kernel composition with the real endpoint and controls for each arm, and the judge/report against faults the composition cannot make. The dev's ablations (A1 hook call removed → `expected 200 to be 409`; A2 report call removed; A3 `unknown` read as `present`; A4 report speaks unless `present`; A5 judge not wired) each go red on the case that owns the behaviour; A1 reproduces the card's bug on the test stack.
- **Must-fix defects on the contract faces: none.** The two correct declaration lines are `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, as the PR carries them. The concurrent-delete window (①.6) is a noted gap for a follow-up card, not a defect of this PR's contract.
